I rarely leave negative reviews, but after what my cat and I went through, I feel obligated to share my experience so other pet owners know when it may be time to seek a second opinion.

My cat suffered from a tail injury for 7 weeks. During that time, I saw three different veterinarians at Companion Animal Hospital, attended multiple appointments (sometimes twice in the same week), followed every recommendation, gave every prescribed medication, and spent approximately $2,000 trying to help him heal.

What was most frustrating was the lack of progress and the lack of a clear plan. Week after week, I was told to continue medications and monitor the wound. Beyond medication, there was very little else recommended. No bandaging, no topical treatments, no alternative wound care plan, just medicine and exposure to air. I trusted the medical advice I was given and followed it exactly, yet after nearly two months the wound remained open and would not heal.

The most disappointing part is that amputation was never seriously discussed until I brought it up myself after 7 weeks of unsuccessful treatment. At that point, I was told a partial amputation would likely solve the issue and that my cat should heal within about two weeks.

Wanting to be certain before putting my cat through surgery, I sought a second opinion. The difference was night and day. Before I even mentioned amputation, the veterinarian immediately explained that because the wound had failed to heal for so long, a partial amputation carried a risk of not solving the problem and could lead to a second surgery later. He recommended a full amputation to give my cat the best chance of healing properly the first time. He also explained that recovery would be closer to a month, not two weeks. It was the first time someone clearly laid out the risks, options, and realistic expectations.

The pricing was also concerning. Gabapentin was nearly double what I have paid elsewhere, and Onsior was significantly marked up as well. I was quoted over $1,650 for an amputation and given a list of supposedly affordable alternatives, only to find many quoted over $2,000. Thankfully, I found a neighborhood veterinarian who immediately identified the problem, provided honest guidance, and performed the surgery.

I understand that veterinary medicine is not always straightforward and that healing cannot be guaranteed. However, after 7 weeks, 3 veterinarians, weekly appointments, thousands of dollars spent, and no meaningful improvement, I expected more proactive communication, more discussion of all available treatment options, and a clearer plan for my pet’s care.

If your pet’s condition is not improving, do not be afraid to seek a second opinion. I wish I had done it much sooner.

In the time my pets visited here:

-My senior cat nearly died because they refilled his thyroid medication at the wrong dose. He lost 30% of his body weight and his fur came out in giant clumps because he was so unwell. This was after I reached out multiple times to express concern that his dose was changed. NO ONE followed up with us to correct this. I had to pay them AGAIN for a re-exam to get his medication filled at the correct dose.

-After my cat had to be put down here they never contacted us to pick up her remains. We were devastated over the holidays to not have her with us. We had to show up in person to get her cremains back and were provided no explanation as to why we were not contacted. NO ONE followed up with us to express regret over this or to provide an explanation.

-At our final visit, the vet tech was so inexperienced and clearly just having a bad day that they were unable to even take my dog's temperature. He was made to be anxious, backed into a corner, and they responded by pushing further and terrifying him. My once happy and compliant dog is now absolutely petrified of the vet. Our new vet has said he has clearly had a traumatic experience and that some animals never recover from this and will forever be fearful of the vet.

I have tried to share this feedback with staff along the way and no one from management or corporate has ever reached out to try and improve upon our experience or make things right. Overall, I am shocked at how inconsiderate and inappropriate our experience here has been. If it's important to you that your pet receive safe doses of their prescriptions, to get their remains back after they die, or for the team to be able to perform a basic physical exam this is not the clinic for you and your pet.

I want to advise everyone… EVERYONE against bringing their pet into this clinic. In May 2025 I brought both of my cats for bloodwork and urine tests due to one having a history of liver inflammation and the other one having urinary crystals. I was very clear at the time of scheduling the appointment that the cats have a long history of health problems and we need a vet who has a lot of experience to take over their care. They told me that the appointment is with Dr. Kung but when we arrived we were seen by Dr. Ryan who is a recent graduate with less than one year of experience. The doctor was unable to handle my cats properly and do a proper exam due to the cats being nervous and trying to escape so no proper exam was done. Then they took them for bloodwork and urine in their cat stroller and gave them back to me soaked in piss and extremely distressed. The entire stroller was soaked in urine. Dr. Ryan wasn’t sure which cat had pissed himself but she assumed that it was Gumbo. Not sure based on what she assumed that. When the technician was removing the bandage from Gumbo’s leg she asked me to hold his head because he already tried to bite her. Gumbo has never tried to bite veterinary staff so that made me question how they handled my cats in order to make them piss themselves and try to bite them. Later that day I called and wanted to file a complaint on a corporate level. The clinic manager called me and apologized for the situation. Said that she will investigate what happened and assured me that urine was collected from both cats because I didn’t believe that if a cat pisses himself he would have any urine for collecting. Today, I was going over the medical records because one of my cats needs to see a vet again and I  just realized that in the other cat’s (Oliver) medical record it clearly stated that he is the one who pissed himself in the carrier which contradicts what dr. Ryan and the manager told me that it was Gumbo. The medical record goes on to say that Oliver’s urine sample was collected from the stroller where he pissed himself. ARE YOU KIDDING ME??? This is a seven year old stroller that has never been washed and the cats have been using it as a cat bed for years. I only wash the blanket inside but not the entire stroller. This urine is totally contaminated and useless! I am also wondering how they collected the urine from the stroller considering that the stroller has a wool blanked and this blanket must’ve absorbed the urine. They blatantly lied to me, didn’t know which cat urinated himself, collected urine from a dirty seven year old stroller. Please so not trust them with your pets at any cost or if you do, do not allow blood, urine or any other procedure to be done without your presence! In my opinion this animal hospital needs to be shut down. I am completely shocked!
